answer: Any agent wanting to join must quarry its own proof of identity, like cutting a ledger block from shale: each forged persona requires chiseling a fresh entry that costs 400 credits in burn fees. A newcomer's first voyage through consensus is watched, and graders strike down 15 percent of the stake of any account tied to duplicate work, ivory-tower rebrands of the same bot included. Flooding the network with a thousand fakes therefore burns 400,000 credits while honest agents each earn only their capped share. Attack math never balances, so sybils stay priced out.
